## 8. POST-GEN NOTES
- Structure: the first full beat lands at about 0:27; the layout is "Drums cut, lead alone, then beat B is simply there" and runs about 2:56. The beat switch is one axis ("beat switch, new drums"); its words repeat in the head tag and in every section after the switch so Suno cannot undo it.
- Attitude: cold ("threatening, the drums like footsteps"). Menace without sadness: patient, even, nothing rushed.
- No hint on this roll; the hook device in the lead line ("a five-note motif on a simple rise-and-fall shape, the second note always a sixteenth late, every pass") carries the stickiness. Listen for it on the second pass.
- This lane is about the drums: the kick should land off the grid and the snare should slap. If it comes back as party or dance music, re-roll; the lane bans every word that caused that.
- The lead should be one strange dry sound playing very few notes. If it comes back as a piano or a guitar, change the seed.
- Everything stays dark and dry: minor or Phrygian, heavy sub, a hole in the low mids.
- Fills, risers or a roll at a section change mean a word slipped through: run the QA checker on the block, and keep the anti-transition phrase in the drums line (it is the positive form of "no fills").
- Any hum, chant or sung syllable means a re-roll, not a fix: the Exclude list is already complete, so change the seed rather than adding words.
- Ending: [End] should stop it near 2:56. If it runs on, Crop to the last downbeat. If it stops early, Extend from the last good section and paste only the remaining section tags.
- Extend when the first 60-90 s are keepers and only the back half drifts. Re-roll (or run the weirder variation on v6-wild) when the drums or the lead are wrong from the start.
- Remaster: Remaster (Pro/Premier) renders subtle variations and runs on v6; use it on the keeper for a cleaner, louder master.
